report.summary: The one-line change lets the native merge gate accept required jobs whose conclusion is `skipped`. In RepositoryCiDO, `skipped` is assigned exactly when a job's need ended without success, so a required job whose dependency failed now passes the gate and the merge proceeds. This contradicts docs/10 Project CI.md ('every `required` job `success`'). The spec is not updated and no test was added.

findings.text: The merge gate now treats `skipped` required jobs as passing. `skipped` is assigned only when a needed job ended without success, so a failed upstream job (e.g. build fails, so required `test` is skipped) no longer blocks the merge. The guard opens instead of staying shut.

evidence.why: pump() runs `if (needs.some((need) => need?.status === "completed" && need.conclusion !== "success")) { this.completeJob(job, "skipped", ...)`, so a required job whose need failed completes as skipped and mergeBlock returns null. The merge then goes ahead although required work never ran. Spec 10 says: 'Merge gate: a native merge needs ... every `required` job `success`.'

findings.text: This changes behavior but the spec is not updated in the same change (CLAUDE.md rule 16). No test covers the new acceptance of skipped jobs (rule 14).

evidence.quote: Merge gate: a native merge needs the newest run for the exact head SHA and the current revision, with every `required` job `success`.
evidence.why: The spec still requires `success`. The code now differs from the spec's source of truth and from docs/CLOUDFLARE-CODE-HOSTING-PLAN.md ('Empty, unknown, incomplete, cancelled, or stale required results cannot grant merge permission').

checked.risk: Spec conformance of the merge gate and job conclusion semantics
Failure paths / guard fails closed: where `skipped` is produced and how the gate consumes it
Security: merge permission granted without required checks running
Repository rules (spec change in same PR, tests for behavior)
Real contracts / idempotency / build environment: not applicable; the change is a pure in-DO predicate over SQLite rows
